records.note: Letter recommending Drew Pinsky for SAMHSA administrator. 'Decisions ... for the public good' names no observable decision, benchmark or threshold; the appointment itself is only a hypothetical antecedent. Nothing can be written as an event.
Whether Pinsky is 'kicked out of' the Republican party is a political-party matter, not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or practice outcome. No formal expulsion mechanism is named either.

Personal and social claims about Pinsky fitting in with celebrities in the new administration and possibly already being friends with Mehmet Oz. Not in the five areas; the 'already friends' clause is a present guess, not a forecast.

Expectation of an 'intervention-style conversation' inside the Trump administration. Internal administration dynamics are not in the five areas, and no observable event can be written from the metaphor.

Recommendation to Makary for 513(g) review-time standards, with predicted consequences: 'more money', industry paying for advice, 'less uncompensated work'. Each is a comparative with no benchmark, series or threshold, and all hinge on the author's own recommendation being adopted by FDA. Regulatory area, but no event can be written.

'Improve the quality of submissions', 'better applications', 'speeds up everything later': comparatives with no benchmark or series, conditional on the author's own 513(g) recommendation being adopted. No event can be written.

'The more FDA can incorporate post-marketing data ..., the better' is a recommendation. The following sentences describe in the present tense what the policy does ('shunts funding', 'moves development'); they assert no future state with a benchmark. No predictive reading survives.

Conditional generality: if approval stays 'too expensive' and therapies are not paid for, investors 'will not put money into them'. Neither the antecedent nor the consequent names an entity, a countable set, a threshold or a series.
'Pharmaceuticals will not be the best way to treat every problem' is a slogan-like generality. 'Best way' has no benchmark and 'every problem' has no countable set.

'Will speed up the process of getting things approved' is a comparative with no benchmark, conditional on the author's own recommendation (industry paying FDA for advice at market rates) and on FDA-CMS coordination. No event can be written.
Conditional on 'getting this part right'; 'capital ... flow into innovations that fail to get anyone healthier' names no entity, countable set, threshold or series.

'A lot of bad behavior in the industry' is a quantifier with no countable set; 'open up the floodgates' is a slogan. The conditional clause ('if the hammer doesn't come down') has no observable antecedent either.

The author's own defamation suit over harassment on Bluesky. A private defamation case about a social network is not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or practice outcome. 'First case to feature Bluesky' also has no named resolution source.
Same lawsuit: the author 'might be the first person to demonstrate' Bluesky's discoverability in court. Private litigation about a social network, outside the five areas.
'I will not be the last' predicts further defamation cases built on Bluesky records. Outside the five areas; also a quantifier with no countable set or deadline.

'Can all live on private servers or hybrid servers in the future' is a capability claim about the federated AT protocol for the #medsky and #academicsky communities. Social-network architecture is outside the five areas, and 'can' states a possibility, not an expectation.
RAMHT is the author's own conference (affiliation: organizer; co-founded with Grady Hannah). The date announcement is a commitment by his own organization.

Claim that Google News alerts will push this newsletter to people with alerts on defamation, Drake, Lamar or Owen Muir. The newsletter's own distribution is outside the five areas; 'everyone who has news alerts' also has no resolution source.
